rows.scope: Recreational boating deaths in New Hampshire in incidents meeting federal reporting criteria, calendar 2025, from the Coast Guard's state tables: Table 30 (51 incidents, 3 of them fatal; 3 deaths; 18 injured) and Table 33 (3 drownings, 0 other deaths, 3 total). The report does not say whether its state tables are by place of incident or state of registration.
rows.source: U.S. Coast Guard, Recreational Boating Statistics 2025, Table 30 p. 67 and Table 33 p. 76
rows.do_not_add_to: A subset of uscg-boating-2025. Recreational boating only; not a count of all New Hampshire drownings; not combined with Maine rows or other years.
rows.note: The drownings figure is the third-last value of the Table 33 row, read under the Drownings, Other Deaths and Total Deaths headings; the alignment is inferred from the extracted text and agrees with Table 30's 3 deaths. A reviewer should confirm it by eye. Found by an independent agent, 23 Nov 2026.

rows.figure: New Hampshire averages 13-15 drownings every year
rows.scope: A state agency's statement of a typical year, in a water-safety news release of 7 Aug 2020. No period, definition (intent, boating, residents) or source is given.
rows.source: New Hampshire Department of Safety, news release 'Be Safe When Enjoying New Hampshire Waters' (7 Aug 2020), issued with Fish and Game and the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
rows.do_not_add_to: An organisation's statement of an average, not a count: not added to or averaged with any yearly count, Maine rows, uscg-boating rows or CDC figures. Replace with official yearly counts when found.
rows.note: The only New Hampshire-wide figure found that a state agency published. The same release says the state had seven drownings so far that year (to 7 Aug 2020). A placeholder until a yearly series is read.

evidence.where: Table 30, Incident, Casualty & Damage Data by State 2025, p. 67 (incidents: total, fatal, non-fatal injury, property damage; deaths; injured; damages)
Table 33, Number of Incidents by Primary Incident Type & State 2025, p. 76, NH row: its last three values (Drownings, Other Deaths, Total Deaths)

evidence.quote: New Hampshire averages 13-15 drownings every year. So far this year, New Hampshire has had seven drownings.

tried: New Hampshire OCME 2017-2019 Biennial Report (https://www.doj.nh.gov/medical-examiner/documents/biennial-report-2017-2019.pdf): no table, caption or sentence mentions drowning; chart contents are images. No later OCME annual report with drowning counts was found; the OCME's other publications found are drug-death summaries.
CDC, Drowning data (https://www.cdc.gov/drowning/data-research/index.html, last reviewed 27 Jan 2026): the state map of 2018-2021 rates is an image; no New Hampshire value appears in the page text.

NH DHHS Injury Prevention page (https://dhhs.nh.gov/programs-services/population-health/maternal-child-health/injury-prevention) points to the DHHS Data Portal Injury Prevention Dashboard, an interactive dashboard: needs a browser; not attempted.
CDC WONDER (ICD-10 W65-W74, V90, V92 filtered to New Hampshire) answers only an interactive session; not attempted.
NH Child Fatality Review Committee annual reports (DHHS) cover children only, mostly in five-year aggregates; not used for an all-ages count.

Press: NHPR (2020, 2022) and the Boston Globe (2023) quote Fish and Game officials giving about a dozen, 13 to 15, or 8 to 12 drownings a year (the last for those Fish and Game handles). Press, so not used.
notes: No official yearly series of New Hampshire drowning deaths was found in a document an automated reader can open. Unlike Maine's, the New Hampshire medical examiner's published reports do not print drowning counts. The two rows are a Coast Guard boating subset for 2025 (grade A) and a state agency's 2020 statement of a typical year (grade C, a placeholder). The yearly series most likely lives in the NH DHHS Injury Prevention Dashboard or CDC WONDER, both interactive; a follow-up task for a person with a browser is proposed. No figures were summed.
